idiom_name: enum Step<T> with Box<dyn FnOnce() -> Step<T>> thunks
implementation_notes: The direct Rust translation of the pattern: a Step<T> enum whose More case owns a boxed FnOnce closure returning the next step, driven by a loop that matches until Done. The closure captures the algorithm state by value, so lifetimes stay local to each step, and Rust 2021 makes the closure and the enum the whole machinery. The price is one heap allocation and one dynamic dispatch per step; the function-pointer variant avoids both when the state fits in a plain value. Rust never guarantees tail-call elimination, so this remains the portable answer for unbounded depth.
pitfalls: Every step boxes a closure, so the driver is a sequence of heap allocations and dynamic calls; a recursive function over a hot path should measure that against the recursion.
A closure that borrows instead of moving does not compile, so state must be owned or shared behind an Arc; fighting that usually means the state wants to be a plain value in a function-pointer step.
Recursion in async fn needs indirection such as Box::pin (stable since Rust 1.77) and still nests polls inside one task, so the async runtime is not a substitute for the driver loop.

variants.name: Allocation-free fn-pointer steps with inline state
variants.idiom_name: enum Step<T, S> carrying fn(S) -> Step<T, S> and the state by value
variants.implementation_notes: A second realization keeps the step as data: the enum stores a plain fn pointer and the state value instead of a boxed closure, so stepping allocates nothing and the driver is monomorphised for the concrete state type. The state must therefore be a single value that the step functions accept and return, which rules out ad-hoc multi-local captures but fits parsers and state machines where the state is already a struct. Choose it over the boxed-closure variant when step cost matters and the algorithm state can be named.
pitfalls: Function pointers cannot capture, so any state the step needs must be passed through the enum payload; forgetting one makes the state type grow into a struct of unrelated fields.
A recursive entry point that is itself part of the mutual group must match the fn-pointer signature exactly, which requires a separate internal function for the first call.
Because the state is copied through the enum, heavy state per step trades allocation for memcpy.
